title: data2vec: A General Framework for Self-supervised Learning in Speech, Vision and Language
layout_note: A wide, short strip in two rows. The left three fifths is a 3 x 2 grid of input examples (columns Images / Speech / Language; top row original, bottom row masked); the right part stacks 'Model in teacher-mode' above 'Model in student-mode', each fed by its row, with two dashed elbow arrows climbing from the student back to the teacher.
grouping: No containers or background panels. Vertical dashed grey rules split the width into four zones: three modality columns with plain headers ('Images', 'Speech', 'Language') and the model zone at right. Rows, not boxes, pair inputs with models: the top row of original examples feeds the teacher and the bottom row of masked examples feeds the student; only the language example in each row sends a solid arrow, standing for all three columns. Two dashed grey elbow arrows leave the student's right edge: the inner one rises to a curly brace under the teacher's two blue layers, labelled 'Predict model representation of original input'; the outer one goes further right, up, and back into the teacher's right edge, labelled 'Teacher tracks student parameters'.
shapes_depth: Flat, nearly monochrome line drawing. Each model is a plain white rectangle with a thin black outline holding three tall narrow outlined bars as layers; the teacher's last two bars are filled solid blue, every other bar is white. Masking is drawn identically in all three modalities as a flat mid-grey square: laid over the photo, replacing a span of the waveform, and standing in for a word of the sentence. Inputs are a real photo, a grey waveform raster and plain text. Arrows are thin grey with small filled heads, solid for data and dashed for training signals.
proposed_highlight: The one saturated colour in the figure marks the targets: the teacher's top layers are filled blue and gathered by a curly brace that the student's prediction arrow points at. Teacher and student are drawn as the same box with the same three layers and told apart only by the title above each ('Model in teacher-mode' / 'Model in student-mode') and by that blue fill.
lesson: One mid-grey square is used as the mask glyph in every modality (over the image, in the waveform, in place of a word), so a single visual idea carries the claim that the same masking applies across inputs.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year (2202.03555); venue as recorded by Semantic Scholar. The figure is mostly white space and thin grey lines; the photos and waveform rasters are the embedded images excluded from the measured palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

arrangement.units: Rows = teacher (top) and student (bottom); columns = the modalities (images, speech, language) separated by dashed vertical rules, then the model column at the right.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo, a waveform and a typed sentence per row, the masked version in the student row
arrangement.losses_at: the prediction target is a dashed arrow from the student block up into the teacher block's outputs, labelled beside it
arrangement.shared: teacher and student drawn as the same block twice, linked by a dashed 'teacher tracks student parameters' loop along the right edge

core.what: the same model drawn twice, teacher-mode above on the unmasked input and student-mode below on the masked input, with a dashed upward arrow from student to the teacher's averaged top layers as the prediction target

relations.form: teacher box directly above student box on the right; a dashed arrow labelled 'Predict model representation of original input' rises from the student into a brace under the teacher's two blue top layers
three modality columns (Images, Speech, Language) separated by dashed vertical rules, each showing an unmasked sample on the top row and the masked version on the bottom row
one long dashed loop on the far right, 'Teacher tracks student parameters', runs from the student's right edge up into the teacher

channels.colour: blue fill = the teacher's top-K layers that form the target; grey boxes = masked regions in every modality; everything else monochrome
channels.shape: tall thin rectangles = transformer layers; a bracketed outer box = one copy of the model
channels.line: solid grey arrow = forward input; dashed grey arrow = training signals (prediction target and the EMA parameter tracking), so dashed carries two different meanings
channels.frame: dashed vertical rules separate modalities; a box frames each model copy

quality.strengths: Real data in each modality (dog photo, waveform, a quoted sentence) with the mask drawn as the same grey block across all three makes the modality-agnostic masking visible; the target is drawn as a brace over the teacher's blue top layers rather than a bare wire.
quality.weaknesses: Only the Language column is wired to the two models, so the image and speech samples float unconnected; dashed lines carry both the regression target and the EMA update; the student's predicted representation is not drawn as an element before the arrow, so what is compared is only half drawn.

insights.structure: Two rows (unmasked on top, masked below) run across three modality columns (Images, Speech, Language) separated by dashed vertical rules, and both rows end in the same model box drawn twice: 'Model in teacher-mode' above, 'Model in student-mode' below.
insights.data: Each modality shows one real sample: a dog photo, a grey waveform and the sentence 'I like tea with milk'; the student row shows the same samples with a grey square pasted over part of each (photo region, waveform span, the word 'with').
insights.emphasis: Only the teacher's top layers are filled blue and gathered by a curly brace, marking that the target is the average of the top-K layer outputs, while the student's layers stay hollow.
insights.flow: Inputs flow left to right by solid arrows only from the Language column into each model; dashed grey arrows go up from the student to the brace ('Predict model representation of original input') and loop round the right side back to the teacher ('Teacher tracks student parameters').
insights.avoid: Only the Language column is wired to the models, so images and speech appear to float unconnected; draw one shared entry for all modalities instead.
